title: Infra GPU fleet, cloud accounts & IaC CI/CD playbook — Addendum
author: Liam Chen
content:
Purpose and context

This addendum supplements the primary infra playbook by capturing operational refinements and newly adopted patterns since the 2026 playbook. It contains updated autoscaler heuristics, image build hardening, and a compact emergency checklist for rapid capacity restoration.

Quick summary of changes
- Autoscaler: added smoothing window and error budget aware backoff to reduce flapping during spot interruptions
- Image pipeline: mandatory CVE scanning stage and image attestation metadata embedded into AMI tags
- Emergency capacity checklist: rapid re-routing steps and temporary traffic shedding thresholds
- CI changes: plan outputs now include resource ownership metadata for faster triage

Updated Autoscaler Guidance
- Goals: reduce scale-flap and improve time-to-recover when spot churn occurs
- New parameters (defaults):
  - smoothing_window = 120s (avg over 2m for queue depth metrics)
  - scale_up_cooldown = 3m
  - scale_down_cooldown = 15m (longer to avoid oscillation)
  - error_budget_backoff = true (if error rate > threshold, increase cooldown and avoid scale-down)
- Best-practice: couple autoscaler decision logs with a short-lived metrics index (1h retention) for quick root cause analysis after incidents

Image Build and Hardening
- Pipeline steps (mandatory):
  - 1) build (packer) -> 2) package signing -> 3) cve-scan (clair/trivy) -> 4) run smoke tests -> 5) attest and tag -> 6) publish to approved image registry
- Image metadata requirements (AMI tags / image labels):
  - image.version, image.build_id, image.built_by, image.cve_scan_status, image.attestation_id
- Rollback note: always keep latest 3 image versions per pool to simplify rollback if a new AMI introduces regressions

Emergency Capacity Restoration Checklist (compact)
1. Identify impact: check per-pool queue depth and P95 latency; determine affected customer tier (hosted/dedicated/private)
2. Immediate mitigation:
   - If interactive routes impacted: enable temporary traffic shedding policy for non-critical routes (shed at 10-20% initially)
   - If autoscaler failed: manually increase pool desired capacity by +25% and verify node provisioning
   - If spot termination caused loss: switch critical pools to reserved instance mix for 30m window and open procurement ticket
3. Communicate: post status in #infra-incident and tag SRE, platform-security, and model-owners for affected models
4. Post-incident: collect autoscaler logs, node lifecycle events, and image metadata; create postmortem within 72h if SLA was violated

CI/CD small but important changes
- Plan diffs now include owner metadata via a new terraform comment convention for resources: "managed_by = 'team:infra;owner:owner@example.com'"
- PR plan summaries include a quick risk score (low/medium/high) computed from number of networking resources changed, IAM resources modified, and cross-account or VPC-route changes
- Canary apply step extended to include a 10-minute passive monitoring window where additional telemetry (KV cache hit ratio, request tail latency) is sampled and compared to baseline

Operational play: cost vs reliability knobs
- Short term (minutes): manual pool sizing, traffic shedding of non-critical routes, temporary switch to reserved capacity
- Medium term (hours): expand pool sizes across AZs, re-route lower-priority workloads to batch pools, engage procurement for reserved capacity
- Long term (days/weeks): revisit sizing model, update headroom percentages, and tune autoscaler thresholds based on observed patterns

Compact runbook: networking regression rollback (2-step)
1. If a networking Terraform apply led to connectivity regressions:
   - Step A: revert the last apply using saved plan or Terraform state snapshot in the prod backend; if revert possible, apply revert and validate connectivity
   - Step B: if revert fails or state is inconsistent, isolate impacted AZ by updating route tables to failover to alternative transit gateway/region; open P1 incident and escalate to network owners

Example emergency CLI snippets
- Manually scale up pool (CLI pseudo-example):
  rwi infra pool scale --pool prod-gpu-us-west-2 --delta +8 --reason "emergency-scale-2026-03-04"
- Fetch latest failed autoscaler logs:
  rwi infra autoscaler logs --pool prod-gpu-us-west-2 --since 1h > /tmp/autoscaler-logs.json

Updated Monitoring & Alerting additions
- New alerts:
  - autoscaler.flap_detected.rate > 0.5 for 15m -> create channel message in #infra-ops (no auto-page first)
  - image.cve_scan_status == "critical" on published AMI -> page infra-security and block image in registry
- Dashboard panels to add:
  - autoscaler decision timeline (events correlated with spot events and scale ops)
  - image rollout map: AMI version per AZ and pool

Appendix: short glossary additions
- Flap: repeated scale up/down cycle within a short window (usually < 10m) causing instability
- Traffic shedding: controlled dropping or queueing of low-priority requests to preserve latency for critical routes
